summary: Quotes are internally consistent, but the episode overclaims: the intervention is confounded across two knobs, 'GRT completes' is treated as success when the record's own facts point to an unresolved physical hotspot, and confidence 0.8 contradicts the episode's own gap list.

findings.claim: Reducing the layer adjustment from 0.45 to 0.2 fixed the congestion.
findings.problem: Confounded intervention: layer adjustment AND congestion iterations (30 to 35) were changed simultaneously. The record says iterations were swept earlier but never states the swept values nor whether 35 alone was tried, so no single-variable attribution is possible.
findings.corrected: After iteration-only attempts (values unrecorded) failed to clear congestion, the member changed the layer adjustment from 0.45 to 0.2 AND raised congestion iterations from 30 to 35, after which GRT completed. Which change mattered is undetermined.

findings.claim: GRT completing constitutes a successful fix.
findings.problem: The record never distinguishes a modeling artifact (0.45 was over-pessimistic; 0.2 reflects reality) from physical congestion. Its own evidence points to the physical case: a localized heatmap hotspot at the top of the die around the macro, plus a separately tracked unresolved cause (net 'looping around the macro', issue #5971). A global capacity-relaxation knob does not fix a localized physical hotspot; it gives the model enough slack to route through it, meaning detailed routing may still fail.
findings.corrected: The intervention relaxes the GRT capacity model's pessimism; it does not address the macro-region hotspot or the looping-net cause, and post-fix detailed-route DRCs were never measured.

findings.problem: Internally inconsistent with the episode's own gaps: no post-fix DRC count, no runtime, no PR link, merge status unknown, closure was automatic not_planned/Stale in 2026, and the actual root cause was deferred to another open issue. A member comment describing a workaround on a ticket later auto-closed stale is not a validated fix.
findings.corrected: confidence 0.3-0.4, labeled 'reported parameter workaround, unmerged and unverified'.

findings.claim: The adjustment of 0.45 is 'too aggressive' and lowering it to 0.2 fixed GRT.
findings.problem: The direction of the parameter's effect is never stated in the record; hypothesis and outcome are mutually consistent only if a higher adjustment means more capacity withheld (more pessimism). The record's own gap admits the meaning is 'only explained in prose'. Also, whether 0.45/0.2 applied to all layers or specific layers is unstated.
findings.corrected: State the semantics explicitly (higher adjustment = larger fraction of routing capacity excluded from GRT's model = more pessimistic estimate) and enumerate which layers or layer ranges the 0.45-to-0.2 change applied to.

findings.problem: Ambiguous in a load-bearing way: either the GRT stage passes, or the entire ORFS flow (including detailed routing) finished. If the latter, a final DRT DRC count necessarily exists, making the absence of any post-state metrics a record-keeping failure rather than merely a gap.
findings.corrected: Post_state must state which reading applies; if the full flow completed, the missing final metrics must be flagged as a recording failure.

findings.claim: 20k routing congestion DRCs at the GRT stage.
findings.problem: Terminology conflation: DRCs are produced by detailed routing; the global router reports congestion/overflow violations. The record contains no detailed-route DRC count anywhere, so 'DRCs' upgrades the observation beyond what was measured.
findings.corrected: Approximately 20,000 global-route congestion/overflow violations reported at the GRT stage; no detailed-route DRC count exists in this record.

findings.claim: Congestion at 'only' 0.24 placement density is paradoxical; 0.45 was 'originally derived from other asap7 designs'.
findings.problem: The juxtaposition invites a false intuition that the record itself resolves: a macro-dominated die with open space at the top can be severely congested in the macro-adjacent channel, since placement density and routing congestion are independent quantities. Separately, the 'originally derived from other asap7 designs' assertion is stated as fact with no citation in the record.
findings.corrected: Drop the 'only' framing or explain that utilization and track-level congestion are independent; mark the provenance of 0.45 as unverified.

findings.problem: Metric undefined: overall die utilization, std-cell placement density target, or post-placement actual are different quantities, and 0.24 is atypically low for a placement-density target, making it more likely a utilization figure.
findings.corrected: Define the metric explicitly or relabel it as die utilization.

corrected_episode.title: BoomTile/Megaboom: ~20k GRT overflow violations at 0.24 die utilization (macro-dominated die, hotspot at top around macro)
corrected_episode.prior_state: BoomTile (Megaboom-derived) in asap7, ORFS v3.0-1735-gdefc349e. Utilization 0.24 with substantial whitespace, concentrated away from the macro region; ORFS aborted at the global-route stage due to residual congestion.
corrected_episode.hypothesis: Two distinct causes kept separate: (1) GRT capacity model possibly over-pessimistic for this design (adjustment 0.45 vs 0.2 used elsewhere; provenance unverified); (2) unresolved physical hotspot - net(s) looping around the macro (issue #5971, deferred, not addressed here).
corrected_episode.chosen_intervention: Two-variable change made together: layer adjustment 0.45 to 0.2 AND congestion iterations 30 to 35. Attribution confessed as confounded.
corrected_episode.post_state: GRT reported to complete per member comment dated 2024-11-14. No re-measured congestion, no detailed-route DRC count, no runtime. Merge status unknown; issue auto-closed not_planned/Stale in 2026. Macro-loop cause remains open in #5971.

notes_for_curator: Do not index this as a 'congestion fixed by parameter tuning' success story. The record shows an unmerged, unverified workaround that sidestepped rather than resolved the suspected root cause. Quotes are authentic and mutually consistent; the mining is sound, the curation is not.
